artifacts.notes: Visually inspected in full on 2026-07-28. The title is printed beneath the scene. Ministers seize or bargain over numerous loaves and fishes spread across a political table; a loaf is labeled Secretary of State, speakers invoke shares and friends, and dogs carry off Pay Office money bags. The changed register is political patronage and appetite, not depiction of Christ's miracle. The print depends on the established Gospel 'loaves and fishes' image, but it does not identify one Synoptic narration; for PC-S42-A it should be described as an afterlife of the feeding tradition appointed in Matthew 14:13-21, not as proof of exclusive dependence on Matthew.
artifacts.rights_basis: The underlying etching was published in 1783 and is public domain in the United States. Wikimedia Commons identifies the exact file as a mechanical scan of the public-domain original, applies the Public Domain Mark, and states that it is free of known copyright restrictions. The British Museum's separate CC BY-NC-SA statement for its supplied digital image is not relied on.

edition.notes: The museum identifies the object as an etching published by E. Achery on 24 March 1783. Its catalogue description records ministers grasping the pictured loaves and fishes as offices and rewards; its curator's note locates the satire in the ministerial interregnum between Shelburne's resignation and the Portland coalition.
edition.title: British Museum object 1868,0808.4955

work.author: Anonymous printmaker; published by E. Achery
work.description: An English political etching published on 24 March 1783. George III presides while past and prospective ministers seize loaves and fishes labeled or understood as government offices and rewards. The Gospel feeding image is converted from provision for a multitude into a satire on political patronage, private appetite, and competition for office.
work.title: The Loaves and Fishes
